Fix unit tests that did not match Molly behavior in the Signal 8.33.2 port

Apply remote config overrides in internal builds. Molly derives internalUser
from the build type, not from the service, so loading overrides must ask
internalUser instead of the service's android.internalUser value, which Molly
does not read. Overrides were never applied before.

Adapt the Signal 8.33.2 tests to intended Molly differences:

- IndividualSettingsViewModelTest stubs getLinkedDeviceCount, which Molly
  adds to the contact details. Molly has no profile badges and no donations,
  so badge and donate clicks produce no action.
- RemoteConfigOverrideTest runs as an internal debug build instead of faking
  the service's internalUser flag.
- NotificationProfileDetailsScreenTest builds the expected schedule text with
  formatHours, since Molly formats times with the locale's best pattern.
- StoryContextMenuTest sets up app dependencies itself rather than relying on
  another test having initialized PartAuthority.
- The app-settings, registration, media-viewer and media-send tests expect
  Molly's music-labelled waves icon, Molly name in the notification warning,
  version row click event, always-shown link device button, a Material 3 theme
  for the Molly video player layout, and Molly's minimum SDK (27).

  restored from Signal. Molly reads these colors from theme attributes and keeps the
  color entries commented out in both color files; the live night-only entries had no

Keep the passphrase timeout when foreground promotion is refused

AI-assisted compatibility changes. The port caught Android's refusal to
promote KeyCachingService to the foreground and continued, where Molly let
the exception propagate. If the service was then destroyed while the process
survived, a later screen-off could miss scheduling the passphrase timeout.
Schedule the configured timeout when promotion is refused and keep it until
promotion succeeds with the screen on and unlocked.

Recover from a failed UnifiedPush registration visibly and boundedly

AI-assisted compatibility changes. A failed distributor registration only
showed a notification and never retried, so UnifiedPush could stay broken
silently. Now the failure shows in UnifiedPush settings with a Retry
registration action, and one automatic UnifiedPushRefreshJob runs per failure
episode (network constraint, three attempts, six-hour lifespan) instead of an
endless background retry. Choosing a distributor, or a successful endpoint
callback, clears the failure. Nothing touches the encrypted store while the
app is locked.
